rv.q: 'It proved incendiary, prompting death threats against the author and necessitating police protection outside the country house he shared with his fiancée, Liccy (played here by Rachael Stirling, sensible and Sloaney, expertly massaging his back and his ego). The situation is an invention.

It’s not depressing to watch though, but by turns hilarious, searing and deeply moving. This is due to Rosenblatt’s multifaceted portrayal of Dahl, interpreted with sublime nuance by Lithgow. The author is physically pained by spinal problems and mentally by noisy renovations at his sun-drenched retreat, Gipsy House in Great Missenden.

First off there’s John Lithgow (also all the awards) stooping and scowling his way into Dahl, charming in his grandpa-ish grumping at the beginning. He’s a walking metaphor: a giant – of literature, of stature – and big.
